title: Methods and protocols for systematic reintroduction of bateng (Bos javanicus)
author: Rattanawat Chaiyarat
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ba8zihx6

steps.title: Prepare and habituate captive banteng
steps.instruction: Maintain seven captive-purebred banteng (four adult males and three adult females, aged 5-7 years) in a 302 ha enclosure with minimal human contact and general medical checkups.

substeps.instruction: Feed animals a diet of Zea mays Linn., Hymenachne pseudointerrupta C. Muell, Hewittia malabarica (L.) Suresh., and Trichosanthes cucumerina L., along with fresh water and artificial salt licks.
Habituate animals individually to transportation boxes (1 m × 2.5 m × 1.8 m, width × long × high) over a period of six months.

steps.title: Immobilize and fit radio collars
steps.instruction: Immobilize the animals using anesthetic drugs and fit them with VHF radio collars (< 3% of body weight, Advanced Telemetry Systems (ATS), Isanti, MN) using standard capture and marking practices prior to transport.

substeps.instruction: Administer Thiafentanil oxalate (0.015 mg/kg) and Medetomidine HCl (0.015 mg/kg) for immobilization.
Use Naltrexone and Atipamizole HCl as reversal drugs.

steps.title: Implement soft release process
steps.instruction: Translocate the banteng to the Salakphra Wildlife Sanctuary and house them in groups in a soft release cage for four months.

substeps.instruction: Switch the diet to natural plants found within the cage, while continuing to provide fresh water and artificial salt licks.
Assess baseline Body Condition Score (BCS) before release.
Test radio collar signals within the soft release cage.

steps.title: Reintroduce animals to the wild
steps.instruction: Release the banteng into the sanctuary in two phases.

substeps.instruction: Reintroduce four individuals in December 2015 (dry season: November to April).
Reintroduce the remaining three individuals in July 2016 (wet season: May to October).

steps.title: Monitor reintroduced banteng via radio tracking
steps.instruction: Track the animals using VHF signals via ground tracking, homing in, and triangulation techniques.

substeps.instruction: Examine collar signals one week after reintroduction to account for habitat unfamiliarity.

steps.title: Install and maintain camera traps
steps.instruction: Install Bushnell 12 MP Trophy Cam HD Essential Trail Cameras between 2016 and 2018 at locations 1 to 3 km apart, primarily at water sources, natural licks, and wildlife trails.

substeps.instruction: Mount cameras on trees at approximately 0.75 m height above ground.
Install two cameras per station facing opposite each other to capture both asymmetrical flanks of the animals.
Set cameras to operate continuously (24 hours/day) with a one-minute shooting interval and a resolution of 1,648 × 1,236 pixels.
Ensure each photograph records Camera ID, time, date, and temperature.
Change memory cards and batteries every month at each location for three years.
